# Verifiers

<!-- GENERATED by devtools.render_verifiers --update from verifiers.yaml, evidence.yaml and results.yaml. Do not edit. -->

Every verification program the evidence register names: the checker each source says it
verified a result with, every program run here or by a third party to confirm one, and
the premise checks that ride with them.
A program is *external* when it was written outside this repository, by a result's
producer or another party, and *first-party* when it was written here.
It *decides* when it decides the claim of the evidence that runs it, and checks
*premises* when it verifies inputs, digests, receipts or a sample and leaves the decision
to another program.

Each evidence entry says how the code that verified it stands to the code its result's
producer used ([`epistemics.md`](../../epistemics.md#confirmation)):

- *reproduced with the producer’s code*: the producer's own checker ran, or, for this project's results, the code
  that produced them;
- *re-implemented, sharing the producer’s components*: separately written code reused named parts of it;
- *independently re-implemented*: code that shares none of it decided the claim.

A replay with the producer's code establishes that the result reproduces, not that a
second implementation agrees.
[`RESULTS.md`](RESULTS.md#verification-code) lists the programs behind each result.

## The Short Version

- **218** programs: **52** external and **166** first-party; **146** decide claims and **72** check premises.
- **673** of **854** evidence entries name the programs that verified them: 319 independently re-implemented, 288 reproduced with the producer’s code, 45 re-implemented, sharing the producer’s components, 21 no relation: a proof, a derivation or a report.

## By Program

### `V-evand-verify-exact`

**verify_exact.py** · Evan Daniel · external · decides · Python · exact-algebraic

The source's standard-library checker of an exact configuration over a number field Q[t]/f: every touching inequality an identity mod f, every other one by rational interval arithmetic at the root of f, each pair separated by a side line or by circumscribed discs, and the side the unique root of p in its interval.

- Source: [`packing/resources/web/evand-exact-and-local-reports-2026-10-12/source/search/exact/verify_exact.py`](../../packing/resources/web/evand-exact-and-local-reports-2026-10-12/source/search/exact/verify_exact.py)
- Versions run: SHA-256 `a0f38ca87c13…`, revision `7d1407a0b66c` (byte-identical at ad86d42, the revision whose packet retains the copy that ran)
- Note: Run unchanged from the retained copy on issue 639's 23 exact forms, each in its own python -I process (receipts/replay-verify-exact.json in the evand-exact-cur-2026-10-16 packet). The replay's evidence entry is added at T-193's stage 4 exit, after the review lane think-7qxm.

### `V-evand-gradec-py`

**gradec.py** · Evan Daniel · external · decides · Python · exact-algebraic

The source's grade-C certificate builder and checker in one program: rows from a contacts file, each tight and classed exactly in Q[t]/f; the flat family and null L0 by exact sparse elimination; affine null vectors for hypothesis 2 of Theorem C; exact multipliers from a linear program's candidate; and the reduced Hessian's leading minors as sums over all permutations, with signs by interval arithmetic at t*. It does not decide that the record is a packing.

- Source: [`packing/resources/web/evand-exact-and-local-reports-2026-10-12/source/search/exact/gradec.py`](../../packing/resources/web/evand-exact-and-local-reports-2026-10-12/source/search/exact/gradec.py)
- Versions run: SHA-256 `61dcf21c2c05…`, revision `ad86d42d0f74` (Git blob 93374b5a4296bfb6d99dd29aa574febcd356e273, byte-identical at 31523f8, the release's tag commit; it imports localmin.py, verify_exact.py and geom.py from its directory, retained beside it.)
- Note: Run here once, at n = 10, from a copy outside the repository on 12 October 2026 (receipts/gradec-n10-recompute.json in the evand-exact-data-2026-10-12 packet), with output byte-identical to the published certificate. The source ran it on all 250 configurations of field degree at most 4 (gradec_runs/run.sh).

### `V-tokoharu-verify-cpp`

### `V-wand125-sqverify-proof-net`

**sqverify-proof-net, the source's adaptation of sqverify-fast, run by fine_net_check.sh** · Hosono, adapting this repository's sqverify_fast · external · decides · Rust, Bash, Python · interval-certified

The source's copy of this repository's sqverify_fast with one change, reading a format M candidate's declared net (proof_net), with which it decides its check2 certificates at every direction of that net; the script runs it with a mass control and writes the receipt.

- Source: [`packing/resources/web/wand125-mixed-bounds-check2-2026-10-06/square-packing-bounds/certificates/mixed_n20_L4905/check2/src/fine_net_check.sh`](../../packing/resources/web/wand125-mixed-bounds-check2-2026-10-06/square-packing-bounds/certificates/mixed_n20_L4905/check2/src/fine_net_check.sh), [`packing/resources/web/wand125-mixed-bounds-check2-2026-10-06/square-packing-bounds/certificates/mixed_n20_L4905/check2/src/SPEC.md`](../../packing/resources/web/wand125-mixed-bounds-check2-2026-10-06/square-packing-bounds/certificates/mixed_n20_L4905/check2/src/SPEC.md)
- Versions run: SHA-256 `a4069c4b55a4…` (fine_net_check.sh, the same in all nine check2 bundles); revision `fe12e036c` (the crate's commit on the source's branch wand125/sqverify-proof-net, which this repository does not hold; its git archive, sqverify-proof-net-fe12e036c.tar.gz, SHA-256 e495f9bf14dc5ca20d8890aa0601183b8b955b94580c4e99ddffa64254371e81, is pinned by the 6 October check2 packet's acquisition record, and its build reports source_sha256 ab6e33e164dbc5c32b40349ba55981b58e630b5eef59534196a69d259404fd7c)
- Note: The crate itself is pinned and neither retained nor opened, so that no copy of it sits beside sqverify_fast, whose own declared-net change was written apart from it (packing/sqverify_fast/INDEPENDENCE.md, Declared Nets). Its SOUNDNESS.md and INDEPENDENCE.md are this repository's files of 3 October by their digests. A replay here by V-sqverify-fast re-implements its check sharing the producer's components, the sqverify_fast crate, all of it but the declared-net reader, not independently; the producer adapted this repository's code, not the reverse, so the replay is much closer to a reproduction than the label alone says.

### `V-check-half-angle-area`

**devtools.check_half_angle_area** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · decides · Python · exact-algebraic

Decides a rational centre and half-angle certificate, or a rational centre-basis witness, in Fraction arithmetic: every rotation on the unit circle, containment in the closed box by each square's half-extent with no corner formed, and disjoint interiors by the circumscribed-disc rule, else by the exact area of one square clipped by the other's four closed half-planes. It reads Evan Daniel's text format, SQUISH's JSON, the centred JSON of issue 483, PingYou Ltd's JSON, Daniil Ostashev's sqcert files, Rio Calle's decimal layouts, rational corners witnesses and derived facts with readers of its own, runs six controls per certificate (two gross, and side and pair each at exact contact and 10^-40 or 10^-30 past it), and holds every side, pose, margin and claimed side to the maintained routes' retained inputs and the record. For issues 470 and 529 it also derives each witness again from its pinned decimal pose or layout file, with its own parser, dilation and half-angle floor in decimal arithmetic, and measures each arrangement against the packing it would be credited to, which decides nothing. Its replay-t128 command drives the kernel's own two-route replay of T-128's receipt.

### `V-couzo-678-replay`

### `V-sqverify-fast`

**sqverify-fast, run at every direction of a certificate's net (the standard 201, the net a format M file declares, or the net a format T file's certificate metadata sets) by devtools.sqverify_fast_census or another first-party driver** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · decides · Rust, Python · interval-certified

Decides a measure-capture lower-bound certificate of format T, M or L on the 201-direction net, of format M on the uniform net its file declares (proof_net, lemma N0), or of format T on the uniform net its certificate metadata sets (D and angle_count, admitted under lemma N0's premises): exact admission of its premises, then an exact-event vertex sweep at the axis and outward-rounded interval branch and bound at every other direction, every shrunk square at every centre of its domain capturing at least the threshold.

- Source: [`packing/sqverify_fast`](../../packing/sqverify_fast), [`packing/devtools/sqverify_fast_census.py`](../../packing/devtools/sqverify_fast_census.py), [`packing/devtools/check_sqverify_fast.py`](../../packing/devtools/check_sqverify_fast.py), [`packing/src/sqpack/rectangle_density.py`](../../packing/src/sqpack/rectangle_density.py)
- Versions run: this repository's commits, which Git holds
- What its authors read and used: [`packing/sqverify_fast/independence-record.yaml`](../../packing/sqverify_fast/independence-record.yaml)
- Note: A clean-room verifier, written from the mathematics without opening the authors' checkers (packing/sqverify_fast/INDEPENDENCE.md), its lemmas proved in packing/sqverify_fast/SOUNDNESS.md, and accepted at 4ddf37d9c by the two adversarial reviews of 3 October 2026, of its soundness and of its testing and independence. Its declared-net change (f007d7afd and 910b6b12c, source_sha256 d97758bb...) was accepted by the soundness review of 6 October 2026 (docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-sqverify-fast-declared-net-soundness.md), for a declared net once the control's exact evaluator read that net (its DR-1), which the same day's re-check confirmed. Its format T metadata-net path, by which a format T file's certificate block sets D and angle_count, has no review of its own: lemma N0 is stated for every net admission accepts, and the review of 10 October 2026 of Guzhou0806's s(40) bound (docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-10-guzhou-n40-clipped-corner-bound.md, its GN-6) read the admission path and every use of the admitted step and found the admitted net used wherever the net enters; admission refuses a metadata net that stops short of pi/4 (control D there). Since 0b5a62ca5 the census driver and the control evaluator read such a net as admission does (that review's GN-5), and no census case holds one yet. Its census drives the binary, keeps every direction's receipt and puts negative controls on a certificate: for format M the original and a near-threshold mutant at its least-bound direction, and since the review of 6 October of FC-1's fix (docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-sqverify-fast-census-control-fc1.md) the 99/100 mutant at every direction of the net, with check_sqverify_fast's exact evaluator and mutation helpers; for format T the original and both mutants at the least-bound leaf centre of least exact capture, evaluated by sqpack.rectangle_density, which was written before the crate and which its authors read (the format T route review of 6 October 2026, docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-sqverify-fast-format-t-route.md). None of these decides coverage. tests/test_sqverify_fast_census.py admits a census row as evidence only for a build of a reviewed source.

### `V-algebraic-witness-reports`

**devtools.algebraic_witness_reports** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · checks premises · Python · exact-algebraic

Imports a packet's algebraic-number-field witnesses from its declaration: derives each witness from its release asset through the manifest the packet pins, holds it to the witness schema, its count and its declared field degree, rebuilds the frozen algebraic claim record against the case records and pending reports, and drives sqpack's exact witness verifier, one route, on a positive and its duplicate-square and outside-container controls per count, writing one receipt per count. It decides no geometry itself.

- Source: [`packing/devtools/algebraic_witness_reports.py`](../../packing/devtools/algebraic_witness_reports.py), [`packing/tests/test_upper_bound_reports_574.py`](../../packing/tests/test_upper_bound_reports_574.py)
- Versions run: this repository's commits, which Git holds
- Note: Written by the import lane of PR 574 on 14 October 2026 for the pull request's algebraic supplement. sqpack.witness.exact_verify decides, over each witness's field; no second route over a number field exists here, and every receipt it writes says so. The review of PR 574 (docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-14-upper-bound-imports-574.md) ran its compare and check --replay and found every job equal to its retained row (RP-3).

### `V-build-field-configuration`

**devtools.build_field_configuration** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · checks premises · Python · exact-algebraic

Builds an exact number-field configuration from a tight rational centre-basis certificate: types its contact graph and refuses an undecided margin, solves the contacts with the side's stationarity (the KKT system) at high precision by mixed-precision Gauss-Newton, pins the directions the side is constant along to small rationals, finds the field's generator and every class tangent in it by integer relation under a full-precision residual test, and solves the centres and the side exactly in the field, refusing unless every contact is an identity there. It decides no feasibility: sqpack's exact witness verifier does, through devtools.algebraic_witness_reports' jobs and controls.

- Source: [`packing/devtools/build_field_configuration.py`](../../packing/devtools/build_field_configuration.py), [`packing/tests/test_build_field_configuration.py`](../../packing/tests/test_build_field_configuration.py)
- Versions run: this repository's commits, which Git holds
- Note: Written by the think-ozx8 import lane on 25 October 2026 to decide issue 804's side at 297 without the author's attachment, from T-174's retained certificate. Its authors read the issue's comments as text (the printed polynomial, the side and the description of the author's field) and none of the author's code; the polynomial is used only as a final comparison, after the side is found in the field (resources/web/hyukdongkim-s297-2026-10-25/README.md, Route A).

No evidence entry names it yet.

### `V-upper-bound-reports`

**devtools.upper_bound_reports** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · checks premises · Python · exact-algebraic

Imports a report of rational upper-bound certificates by another author from its packet's declaration: admits custody through acquire_source, reads each retained file or derived fact by its declared adapter (Evan Daniel's text format, SQUISH's JSON, centred JSON, PingYou Ltd's JSON, Daniil Ostashev's sqcert files, Rio Calle's decimal layouts, rational corners witnesses, decimal poses by a declared dilation, Joost de Winter's centre-basis JSON), holds a derived fact to any file its row names as the same packing, admits each side only where it equals or rounds up to its print, rebuilds the frozen claim comparison and the register plan, and drives the arrangement kernel's two exact routes and two controls per count. It decides no geometry itself.

- Source: [`packing/devtools/upper_bound_reports.py`](../../packing/devtools/upper_bound_reports.py), [`packing/devtools/evand_arrangement_reports.py`](../../packing/devtools/evand_arrangement_reports.py), [`packing/tests/test_upper_bound_reports.py`](../../packing/tests/test_upper_bound_reports.py)

### `V-review-1023-n31-capture`

**capture.py, with n31_geometry.py, n31_exact.py and n31_brute.py** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · decides · Python · exact-algebraic

Decides the capture condition of a format M measure on a declared net at the directions it is given, over the whole quadrant [L/2, L - r(a_j)]^2 of centres: a branch and bound on the kernel-and-slab cell bound (exact to first order in the cell's size), chosen by a float64 pass and decided leaf by leaf in exact integers (densities rounded down to 2^-64, the domain's upper end rounded up), with the leaves checked to partition the quadrant. ### `V-kaggle-268-304-review-check`

**t241_t242_exact.py** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · decides · Python · exact-algebraic

The 24 October review's standard-library exact checker of the three certificates T-241 and T-242 cite (Francisco Couzo's 304 at fa6237e, Evan Daniel's 268 and 304 at 8a8879a), with a reader of its own that admits only integer and p/q literals and the stated row count, deciding each certificate in Fraction arithmetic by two methods: separating axes (every corner against the walls, and every pair whose centres lie within 2 of each other, chosen exactly, on the four edge normals; the rest disjoint by their circumscribed discs) and clipped areas (Sutherland-Hodgman: each square clipped to the box keeps area 1, each near pair's intersection has area 0), with a third pass of separating axes over every pair. ### `V-register-candidates`

**devtools.register_candidates** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · checks premises · Python · exact-algebraic

Retains this project's certificates below a case's house best packing as a batch: a regularization run's solve certificate, at the side the run's retained report records, or a construction of one L strip of unit squares added to an import packet's certificate at a smaller count, rebuilt from that packet wherever it is read and held to the retained file pose for pose. The replay command decides the certificates and the tests hold their custody (tests/test_register_candidates.py). It drives the arrangement kernel's three jobs and the six sharp controls of devtools.upper_bound_sharp_controls on both maintained exact routes and writes their receipts. It decides no geometry itself.

### `V-configuration-fact-replay`

**devtools.configuration_fact_replay** · Squares Project (Levy) · first-party · checks premises · Python · exact-algebraic

Reads Hyukdong Kim's exact configurations for T-244, kept as derived JSON facts: rebuilds the author's file byte for byte from each and records its digest, which tests/test_configuration_fact_replay.py holds to the one the comment states, checks that its side is T-244's (the same irreducible polynomial, a root of it in K, and one root in the hull of both isolating intervals, counted by SymPy), turns it into a centre-basis Witness/v2 over K through devtools.algebraic_witness_reports.evand_minpoly_geometry, drives sqpack's exact verifier on a positive and two controls, and runs the source's verify_exact.py unchanged on the rebuilt file and on four mutated controls.
